note: Episode 1 (Book I, chapters I–XIX). Recipe (18 Nov, Ian): gemini-2.5-flash-image, alla-prima style sentence, face portraits only as references, no style-plate image.
style: An oil painting of 58 BC, in the manner of Jean-Léon Gérôme, Lawrence Alma-Tadema and Ernest Meissonier's military pictures, painted alla prima: visible loose brushstrokes, thick impasto in the lights, thin transparent glazes in the shadows, soft lost edges away from the faces, broken colour, canvas weave showing through; brilliant Mediterranean and Gaulish daylight — deep blue sky, towering white clouds, raking sun and crisp blue shadow on warm earth and stone (at night or by fire: a single source of light, much of the picture in deep shadow); ordinary, unidealised faces, not glamorous, painted in a few planes; a candid, unposed moment, figures off-centre. Roman legionaries in mail shirts, bronze Montefortino helmets and curved oval shields; Gauls with long hair, moustaches, checked trousers, cloaks and torcs. Not an illustration, not digital art. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: A vast painted bird's-eye view of all Gaul in 58 BC seen from high above the Alps on a clear day: the great rivers Rhône, Saône, Loire, Seine and Garonne winding north and west through forests and plains toward a far silver ocean, the Pyrenees to the south-west, the Rhine and dark German forests to the north-east. No people, no lettering.

A dark oak forest in northern Gaul: Belgic warriors with long limed hair, moustaches, spears and tall oval shields gathered in a clearing, smoke from a hall; across a river the edge of German forest. Any people are small, far off, with no detail in their faces.

The Garonne river winding through the warm south-west of Gaul toward the snowy Pyrenees on a bright day, a small Aquitanian village of thatched houses, herds on the meadows. Any people are small, far off, with no detail in their faces.

The land of the Helvetii from the heights of the Jura on a brilliant summer day: Lake Geneva shining below, the Rhône leaving it, and the Alps white beyond; farms and villages in the green valleys. Any people are small, far off, with no detail in their faces.

Inside a great timber hall of the Helvetii by firelight and daylight from the smoke-hole: Orgetorix, a rich Helvetian noble with long hair, moustache, gold torc and a fur-trimmed checked cloak, swears an oath with a ring of nobles, their hands on a sword.Roman legionaries wear mail shirts, bronze Montefortino helmets and curved oval shields; Gauls have long hair, moustaches, checked trousers, cloaks and torcs.

A wide summer valley of the Helvetii filled with hundreds of wagons with solid wheels, oxen and draught horses being gathered, men loading sacks of grain, women and children, fields being sown; mountains beyond. Any people are small, far off, with no detail in their faces.

On a hillside above a river, Orgetorix of the Helvetii clasps hands with Dumnorix of the Aedui and with Casticus of the Sequani, three Gaulish chiefs in rich cloaks and torcs swearing a secret pact, their horsemen waiting below.Roman legionaries wear mail shirts, bronze Montefortino helmets and curved oval shields; Gauls have long hair, moustaches, checked trousers, cloaks and torcs.

A Helvetian assembly in an open meadow: Orgetorix led forward in chains before the magistrates, while a huge crowd of his retainers, ten thousand armed men, surges behind him with spears; overcast sky. Any people are small, far off, with no detail in their faces.

Night in a Helvetian town: torches and armed men in the streets, the magistrates gathering a force, a chieftain's house dark; moonlight on thatched roofs. Any people are small, far off, with no detail in their faces.

The Helvetii burn their own towns and villages before leaving: a whole valley of thatched towns in flames under a towering column of smoke at sunset, a long column of wagons already moving away along the road. Any people are small, far off, with no detail in their faces.

A narrow, difficult pass between the steep cliffs of the Jura and the river Rhône, scarcely wide enough for single wagons, a high mountain overhanging it; a few figures and a cart far below. Any people are small, far off, with no detail in their faces.

The town of Geneva of the Allobroges at the end of Lake Geneva in 58 BC: a small hill town with timber walls, the wooden bridge over the Rhône leading toward the Helvetian shore, the Alps beyond under a blue sky. Any people are small, far off, with no detail in their faces.
